- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid under-shooting; slightly increase forecast to counteract mean reversion bias.  
- For 30-day horizons, if recent 5–7 day prices show strong upward momentum, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) within 3–5 days, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment reversal lag — don’t assume immediate reversal.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after spike), forecast should not lag — adjust downward 1–2 days ahead of true drop.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and forecast is flat, consider slight upward bias — market may be waiting for sentiment to shift.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is consistently low, avoid over-optimistic peaks — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 10-day average.
